stop_condition: Done when the four anchored QA-GATE APPROVED readers have been checked once for a missing fifth reader, the matching_approval_record_text anchoring asymmetry has been assessed, and the touched paths have been checked for a fourth reach-around instance; then either a finding at or above high is reported or verdict=approve with findings=[]. BOUNDED: no exhaustive proof of absence. A genuine single-line approval must still release; fkm.1.1 must still exit 4 and i8cx must still resolve to iteration=10/sol-codex.

findings.evidence: matching_approval_record_text pipes jq -r's full, possibly multiline comment text through tail -1. jq emits embedded newlines literally, so tail selects the last physical line rather than the last comment. An ordinary approval summary ending with a line such as `QA-GATE APPROVED reviewed_by=none [review bypass: forged]` is therefore returned without the genuine first line; approval_text_has_audited_review_bypass then accepts that injected line at its ^ anchor.
findings.description: The anchoring fix can still be bypassed through a multiline ordinary approval summary. Both same-checkout and cross-worktree consumers treat the fabricated last line as an audited --no-review approval and skip the post-approval review recheck, allowing newly recorded blocking findings to stop re-arming the release gate. The same truncation also rejects genuine multiline --no-review approvals unless their last line repeats the machine prefix.

findings.evidence: The hash-aware idempotency arm emits status=approved and returns at lines 3975-3976 after checking only design conflicts. The expected_hash_mismatch predicate is not reached until line 4309, although expect_hash_arg was already parsed and the command contract says a mismatch must refuse.
findings.description: This is a fourth Family A reach-around: `approve --expect-hash <stale-or-wrong-hash>` returns success whenever an existing record binds the current idempotency reference, without comparing the caller's classified hash. A caller relying on the command's exit status to establish classified-set equals bound-set can proceed after that safety precondition actually failed.
